questions.topicName: Viral Hepatitis: Presentation, Diagnosis, and Autoimmune Comparison
questions.stem: A 24-year-old man is evaluated at his physician's office before starting a job that requires documentation of hepatitis B status. He feels well and takes no medications. Serologic testing shows: HBsAg negative, anti-HBs negative, anti-HBc total positive, anti-HBc IgM negative, and HBV DNA not detected. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for these results?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Immunity induced by prior hepatitis B vaccination

choices.label: B
choices.text: Remote resolved hepatitis B virus infection

choices.label: C
choices.text: Acute hepatitis B during the window period

choices.label: D
choices.text: Active chronic hepatitis B virus infection

choices.label: E
choices.text: Passive immunity from recent immune globulin

explanation.summary: Isolated anti-HBc (total) with negative HBsAg, anti-HBs, and DNA usually means remote resolved HBV whose anti-HBs has waned.
explanation.whyCorrect: Anti-HBc total positivity with a negative HBsAg, negative anti-HBs, negative IgM, and undetectable DNA most often reflects remote resolved infection in which protective anti-HBs has fallen below the detection threshold.

whyWrongByChoice.A: Vaccination produces isolated anti-HBs positivity, not anti-HBc, since vaccine contains only surface antigen.
whyWrongByChoice.C: The acute window period is defined by a positive anti-HBc IgM, which is negative here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Active chronic infection requires persistent HBsAg (and usually detectable DNA), both negative here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Immune globulin gives passive anti-HBs, not anti-HBc, and there is no such exposure history.

questions.topicName: Viral Hepatitis: Presentation, Diagnosis, and Autoimmune Comparison
questions.stem: A 46-year-old woman with a 6-year history of a chronic bloodborne viral infection comes to the clinic with palpable purpura on the legs, arthralgias, and numbness of both feet. Laboratory studies show a low C4, positive rheumatoid factor, and serum proteins that precipitate when the sample is refrigerated. Urinalysis shows dysmorphic red cells and red-cell casts. Which of the following best explains her renal findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Immune complex deposition in glomerular capillaries

choices.label: B
choices.text: Antibodies directed against the basement membrane

choices.label: E
choices.text: Amyloid fibril deposition within the mesangium

explanation.summary: Chronic HCV drives mixed cryoglobulinemia → membranoproliferative GN from immune-complex deposition.
explanation.whyCorrect: The chronic bloodborne virus with cryoglobulins, low C4, purpura, and a nephritic sediment is hepatitis C with mixed cryoglobulinemia, which causes membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis via immune-complex deposition in glomerular capillaries.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Anti–basement membrane antibodies cause Goodpasture disease with linear IgG, not cryoglobulinemic GN.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Isolated foot-process effacement without deposits is minimal change disease, which is not immune-complex mediated.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Nodular glomerulosclerosis (Kimmelstiel-Wilson) is diabetic nephropathy, not a cryoglobulinemic process.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Amyloid deposition produces nephrotic-range proteinuria with Congo-red positivity, not this nephritic cryoglobulinemic picture.

questions.topicName: Viral Hepatitis: Presentation, Diagnosis, and Autoimmune Comparison
questions.stem: A 30-year-old woman at 30 weeks of gestation is found on prenatal screening to be HBsAg positive and HBeAg positive, with an HBV DNA level of 2 × 10^8 IU/mL. She feels well and her ALT is normal. Plans are made to give the newborn hepatitis B immune globulin and vaccine at birth. Which of the following is the most appropriate additional step for the mother?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Give the mother immune globulin now

choices.label: E
choices.text: Administer a maternal hepatitis B booster

explanation.summary: High maternal HBV DNA: third-trimester tenofovir lowers viral load and further cuts perinatal transmission beyond newborn HBIG + vaccine.
explanation.whyCorrect: With a high maternal viral load, third-trimester tenofovir reduces HBV DNA and lowers residual perinatal transmission risk that persists even with newborn immunoprophylaxis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Cesarean delivery does not reliably reduce HBV transmission and is not indicated for viral load alone.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Maternal immune globulin does not lower her viral load and is not part of transmission prevention here.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Antiviral must lower the viral load before delivery; starting after delivery misses the transmission window, and entecavir is not preferred in pregnancy.
whyWrongByChoice.E: A maternal booster does not reduce her circulating viral load or transmission risk.

questions.topicName: Viral Hepatitis: Presentation, Diagnosis, and Autoimmune Comparison
questions.stem: A previously healthy 40-year-old man is brought to the emergency department with fever, confusion, and jaundice that have worsened over 4 days. Serum AST is 4,900 U/L, ALT is 5,200 U/L, and INR is 3.4. Hepatitis A, B, and C serologies are negative and the acetaminophen level is undetectable. He is becoming encephalopathic. Which of the following is the most appropriate empiric pharmacotherapy to begin now?

explanation.summary: Fulminant hepatitis of unknown cause: give empiric acyclovir for possible HSV before PCR confirmation.
explanation.whyCorrect: HSV hepatitis is a rare but rapidly fatal cause of fulminant liver failure that must not be missed. Because it is treatable and lethal if delayed, empiric IV acyclovir is started before HSV PCR results return.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ceftriaxone treats bacterial infection, which is not the treatable lethal cause suggested by fulminant hepatitis of unclear origin.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Corticosteroids treat autoimmune hepatitis and could worsen an undiagnosed viral infection.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Entecavir treats chronic hepatitis B, which is serologically excluded here.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fluconazole treats candidiasis, not the HSV possibility that empiric therapy must cover.

questions.topicName: Viral Hepatitis: Presentation, Diagnosis, and Autoimmune Comparison
questions.stem: A 60-year-old man with lymphoma has baseline serologies of HBsAg negative, anti-HBc positive, and anti-HBs positive. He begins rituximab-based chemotherapy without antiviral prophylaxis. Four months later his ALT rises sharply, HBV DNA becomes strongly positive, and HBsAg is now detectable. Which of the following best explains this change?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Reactivation of previously controlled HBV infection

choices.label: B
choices.text: Newly acquired acute hepatitis B infection

choices.label: D
choices.text: Autoimmune hepatitis triggered by the lymphoma

explanation.summary: B-cell depletion removes immune control of latent HBV → reactivation with HBsAg seroreversion.
explanation.whyCorrect: Resolved HBV persists as covalently closed circular DNA in hepatocytes. Rituximab depletes B cells and removes immune control, allowing reactivation with reappearance of HBsAg and rising HBV DNA — the reason prophylaxis is given in anti-HBc–positive patients.

whyWrongByChoice.B: A new acute infection is unlikely given his prior resolved-infection serologies; this is recrudescence of his own virus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Direct chemotherapy toxicity would not turn HBsAg and HBV DNA positive.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Autoimmune hepatitis does not produce a positive HBsAg or rising HBV DNA.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Hepatocellular carcinoma does not cause HBsAg seroreversion with a viral-load surge.

questions.topicName: Viral Hepatitis: Presentation, Diagnosis, and Autoimmune Comparison
questions.stem: A 35-year-old man who has been HBsAg positive for 5 years develops abrupt worsening of jaundice and a steep rise in transaminases over 2 weeks. Testing is now positive for anti-HDV and HDV RNA. Compared with his prior stable course, which of the following outcomes is most likely?

choices.label: D
choices.text: Complete resolution within a few weeks

choices.label: E
choices.text: Conversion to an inactive carrier state

explanation.summary: HDV superinfection of a chronic HBV carrier accelerates progression to severe disease and cirrhosis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hepatitis D superinfection in an established chronic HBV carrier characteristically causes severe hepatitis with a high rate of chronic HDV and accelerated progression to cirrhosis.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Surface antigen clearance signals resolution, the opposite of the aggressive course superinfection produces.
whyWrongByChoice.C: HDV superinfection does not confer protective immunity; it worsens disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Prompt resolution characterizes some acute coinfections, not superinfection of a chronic carrier.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Superinfection drives active severe disease rather than an inactive carrier state.

questions.topicName: Viral Hepatitis: Presentation, Diagnosis, and Autoimmune Comparison
questions.stem: A 24-year-old man comes to the clinic with 5 days of malaise, nausea, and jaundice after returning from travel to a region with poor sanitation, where he drank untreated water. Anti-HAV IgM is positive. His two unvaccinated household contacts feel well. Which of the following is most appropriate to protect the household contacts?

explanation.summary: Post-exposure prophylaxis for household contacts of acute hepatitis A is the hepatitis A vaccine.
explanation.whyCorrect: For close contacts of a person with acute hepatitis A, post-exposure prophylaxis with the hepatitis A vaccine (with immune globulin in selected patients) prevents secondary fecal-oral spread.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hepatitis B vaccine does not protect against the fecal-orally transmitted hepatitis A virus.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Acyclovir treats herpesviruses and has no role in hepatitis A prophylaxis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ribavirin is not used for hepatitis A, which is self-limited and vaccine-preventable.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Contacts are at real risk of fecal-oral transmission, so prophylaxis is warranted rather than observation.

questions.topicName: Viral Hepatitis: Presentation, Diagnosis, and Autoimmune Comparison
questions.stem: A 52-year-old man undergoes liver biopsy for chronically elevated transaminases. The biopsy shows hepatocytes with pale, finely granular 'ground-glass' cytoplasm caused by accumulation of a viral product in the endoplasmic reticulum. Elevation of which of the following serum markers would most likely accompany this finding?

explanation.summary: Ground-glass hepatocytes are packed with HBsAg; serum HBsAg is the correlating marker.
explanation.whyCorrect: Ground-glass hepatocytes result from HBsAg accumulating in the endoplasmic reticulum, so detectable serum HBsAg is the marker that correlates with the stored substance.

whyWrongByChoice.B: HBeAg reflects replication and infectivity, not the surface antigen filling ground-glass cells.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Anti-HBs indicates immunity or resolution and would not accompany active HBsAg-laden hepatocytes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Anti-HCV IgG marks hepatitis C, which does not produce ground-glass change.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Anti-HAV IgM marks acute hepatitis A, unrelated to this chronic HBV finding.

questions.topicName: Viral Hepatitis: Presentation, Diagnosis, and Autoimmune Comparison
questions.stem: A 34-year-old man who received a kidney transplant 6 weeks ago is admitted with fever and elevated transaminases. Liver biopsy shows enlarged cells containing large intranuclear inclusions surrounded by a clear halo. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

explanation.summary: Owl's-eye intranuclear inclusions in a transplant recipient indicate CMV → treat with ganciclovir.
explanation.whyCorrect: The large 'owl's-eye' intranuclear inclusions in an immunosuppressed transplant recipient indicate cytomegalovirus, which is treated with ganciclovir (or valganciclovir).

whyWrongByChoice.B: Acyclovir has poor activity against CMV; it treats HSV/VZV, which do not give owl's-eye inclusions in this setting.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Praziquantel treats trematodes, not a viral inclusion-body hepatitis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Entecavir treats hepatitis B, which does not produce owl's-eye intranuclear inclusions.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Metronidazole treats amebic infection, not CMV.

questions.topicName: Viral Hepatitis: Presentation, Diagnosis, and Autoimmune Comparison
questions.stem: A 27-year-old woman at 32 weeks of gestation returns from travel to an area with poor sanitation and develops jaundice, nausea, and markedly elevated transaminases. Serologic testing is positive for anti-HEV IgM. Which of the following complications is she at greatest risk of developing?

explanation.summary: Hepatitis E carries a markedly increased risk of fulminant hepatic failure specifically in pregnancy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hepatitis E is usually acute and self-limited, but in pregnant women it carries a markedly increased risk of fulminant (acute) hepatic failure.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Chronic hepatitis from HEV occurs mainly in immunocompromised hosts, not in this acute pregnancy setting.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Hepatocellular carcinoma follows years of chronic HBV/HCV or cirrhosis, not acute HEV.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Progressive cirrhosis develops over years of chronic injury, not from acute self-limited HEV.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Biliary carcinoma is linked to chronic biliary fluke infection, not to acute hepatitis E.

questions.topicName: Viral Hepatitis: Presentation, Diagnosis, and Autoimmune Comparison
questions.stem: A 29-year-old nurse sustains a needle-stick injury from a patient who is HBsAg positive. She completed the hepatitis B vaccine series several years ago and has a documented anti-HBs titer of 45 mIU/mL. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step for hepatitis B?

explanation.summary: A documented anti-HBs ≥10 mIU/mL means she is an immune vaccine responder — no post-exposure treatment.
explanation.whyCorrect: A prior anti-HBs titer ≥10 mIU/mL defines an immune responder who is protected, so no immune globulin or additional vaccination is needed after HBV exposure.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Immune globulin plus revaccination is for documented non-responders, not a proven responder.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Immune globulin adds nothing when protective anti-HBs is already present.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A repeat series is unnecessary in someone with a documented protective titer.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Antiviral prophylaxis is used for HIV exposures, not for HBV in an immune responder.

questions.topicName: Viral Hepatitis: Presentation, Diagnosis, and Autoimmune Comparison
questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman comes to the office with 1 week of fatigue and jaundice. Serum AST is 780 U/L and ALT is 900 U/L, while alkaline phosphatase is 110 U/L (normal) and total bilirubin is 6 mg/dL. She drinks no alcohol and takes no medications. Which of the following is the most appropriate next diagnostic step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Hepatitis A, B, and C serologic testing

explanation.summary: A strongly hepatocellular pattern (very high transaminases, normal ALP) points to viral/autoimmune hepatitis workup, not biliary imaging.
explanation.whyCorrect: The markedly elevated transaminases with a normal alkaline phosphatase indicate a hepatocellular rather than cholestatic process, so viral hepatitis serologies (the most common cause) are the appropriate first workup.

whyWrongByChoice.B: ERCP evaluates biliary obstruction, which the normal alkaline phosphatase argues against.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Ultrasound targets a cholestatic/obstructive picture, not this hepatocellular pattern.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Antimitochondrial antibody screens for primary biliary cholangitis, a cholestatic disease with a high ALP.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ceruloplasmin/urine copper screen for Wilson disease, a less likely first consideration than viral hepatitis here.

questions.topicName: Viral Hepatitis: Presentation, Diagnosis, and Autoimmune Comparison
questions.stem: A 33-year-old woman comes to the clinic with fatigue and jaundice. Serum ALT is 640 U/L, viral hepatitis serologies are negative, and she drinks no alcohol. Additional studies show elevated serum IgG with positive antinuclear and anti–smooth muscle antibodies, and liver biopsy shows interface hepatitis with a plasma-cell–rich infiltrate. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

explanation.summary: Negative viral serologies with high IgG, ANA/ASMA, and plasma-cell interface hepatitis define autoimmune hepatitis → prednisone + azathioprine.
explanation.whyCorrect: The picture is autoimmune hepatitis, treated with immunosuppression: prednisone to control inflammation plus azathioprine as a steroid-sparing agent, which improves long-term survival.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Ledipasvir-sofosbuvir treats hepatitis C, which is serologically negative here.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Tenofovir and entecavir treat hepatitis B, also excluded by negative serologies.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ursodiol/cholestyramine target cholestatic disease (e.g., PBC), not autoimmune hepatitis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Rifaximin/lactulose treat hepatic encephalopathy, not the underlying autoimmune inflammation.

questions.topicName: Viral Hepatitis: Presentation, Diagnosis, and Autoimmune Comparison
questions.stem: A 26-year-old woman completed a 12-week course of direct-acting antiviral therapy for hepatitis C 6 months ago. Today her HCV RNA is undetectable but her anti-HCV IgG remains positive. She asks what this means for her future. Which of the following statements is most accurate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: She is cured but can be reinfected later

choices.label: B
choices.text: She has active infection despite treatment

choices.label: C
choices.text: She now has lifelong protective immunity

choices.label: D
choices.text: She requires an additional treatment course

choices.label: E
choices.text: She has developed a chronic HCV infection

explanation.summary: Undetectable HCV RNA after DAAs = cure; anti-HCV IgG persists but is not protective, so reinfection is possible.
explanation.whyCorrect: An undetectable HCV RNA after therapy indicates cure (sustained virologic response). Anti-HCV IgG persists as a marker of past infection but does not confer immunity, so reinfection can occur with new exposures.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Undetectable RNA indicates cleared virus; the persistent antibody reflects past, not active, infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Unlike anti-HBs, anti-HCV antibodies are not protective.
whyWrongByChoice.D: A persistent antibody after cure is expected and does not indicate a need to re-treat.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Chronic infection would show detectable HCV RNA, which is absent here.

questions.topicName: Infectious Hepatic Abscesses and Flukes
questions.stem: A 42-year-old man comes to the emergency department with 3 weeks of fevers and right upper quadrant pain after returning from rural Mexico. CT shows a single well-defined cyst in the right hepatic lobe, and serum Entamoeba histolytica serology is positive. He is started on metronidazole and improves. Which of the following should be added to prevent relapse?

explanation.summary: After metronidazole clears invasive amebae, a luminal agent (paromomycin) eradicates intestinal cysts and prevents relapse.
explanation.whyCorrect: Metronidazole kills invasive trophozoites in the liver but not the intestinal luminal cysts that cause relapse. A luminal agent such as paromomycin is added to eradicate colonization.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Praziquantel treats trematodes, not Entamoeba.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fluconazole treats Candida abscesses, not amebiasis.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Ceftriaxone covers bacteria, not the intestinal amebic cysts driving relapse.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Albendazole treats echinococcal and some nematode disease, not amebic colonization.

questions.topicName: Infectious Hepatic Abscesses and Flukes
questions.stem: A 58-year-old man with recent ascending cholangitis develops fever and several small hepatic abscesses on imaging. Blood cultures grow a gram-negative rod. He is started on broad-spectrum antibiotics. Which of the following is the most important additional intervention?

explanation.summary: Pyogenic abscess from ascending cholangitis needs source control: drainage and relief of the biliary obstruction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Pyogenic hepatic abscesses arising from ascending biliary disease require antibiotics plus source control — drainage and relief of the underlying biliary obstruction — without which infection persists.

whyWrongByChoice.B: The biliary source and gram-negative bacteremia indicate a pyogenic, not parasitic, process.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Amebic serology would delay needed source control in a clearly pyogenic biliary-source abscess.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Antifungal therapy targets Candida microabscesses, not this bacterial biliary infection.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Transplantation is not indicated for a drainable infection with a treatable biliary source.

questions.topicName: Infectious Hepatic Abscesses and Flukes
questions.stem: A 47-year-old man who emigrated from Southeast Asia comes to the clinic with chronic right upper quadrant discomfort and peripheral eosinophilia. He frequently eats raw freshwater fish. Imaging shows intrahepatic biliary dilation and ductal wall thickening. Long-standing infection with the responsible organism most increases the risk of which of the following?

explanation.summary: Clonorchis (raw freshwater fish) chronically inflames bile ducts, raising cholangiocarcinoma risk.
explanation.whyCorrect: The exposure and biliary findings indicate Clonorchis sinensis, which inhabits the biliary tree and causes chronic ductal inflammation predisposing to cholangiocarcinoma.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Hepatocellular carcinoma follows chronic viral hepatitis and cirrhosis, not biliary fluke infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Gallbladder carcinoma is linked to chronic cholelithiasis, not to this ductal fluke.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Pancreatic carcinoma is not the malignancy associated with liver flukes.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Colorectal carcinoma is unrelated to biliary fluke infection.

questions.topicName: Infectious Hepatic Abscesses and Flukes
questions.stem: A 40-year-old woman comes to the clinic with right upper quadrant pain, intermittent fever, and marked peripheral eosinophilia. She lives on a farm and regularly eats wild watercress from a nearby stream. Imaging shows tracks within the liver extending toward the biliary tree. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause?

explanation.summary: Watercress ingestion with eosinophilia and hepatic migratory tracks indicates Fasciola hepatica.
explanation.whyCorrect: Fasciola hepatica is acquired from aquatic vegetation such as watercress; larvae migrate through the liver parenchyma toward the biliary tree, producing eosinophilia and migratory tracks.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Clonorchis is acquired from raw freshwater fish, not watercress.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Schistosoma mansoni is acquired by freshwater skin penetration and causes periportal fibrosis, not watercress-borne biliary disease.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Entamoeba causes a solitary abscess from fecal-oral spread, not migratory tracks with eosinophilia.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Echinococcus is acquired from dog tapeworm eggs and forms hydatid cysts, not migratory tracks.

questions.topicName: Infectious Hepatic Abscesses and Flukes
questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman receiving induction chemotherapy for acute leukemia has persistent fevers despite broad-spectrum antibiotics. As her neutrophil count recovers, imaging shows multiple tiny abscesses scattered through the liver and spleen. Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?

explanation.summary: Multiple hepatosplenic microabscesses in a recovering neutropenic patient with antibiotic-refractory fever indicate hepatosplenic candidiasis.
explanation.whyCorrect: Candida causes multiple small hepatic and splenic microabscesses, classically becoming apparent as neutrophils recover in a patient whose fevers persisted despite antibacterial therapy.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Entamoeba produces a solitary right-lobe abscess in a traveler, not scattered microabscesses in neutropenia.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clonorchis infects the biliary tree from raw fish and does not cause hepatosplenic microabscesses.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Klebsiella pyogenic abscesses are usually few and larger and arise from biliary or portal sources.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Fasciola is a biliary fluke from watercress, not a cause of hepatosplenic microabscesses.

questions.topicName: Infectious Hepatic Abscesses and Flukes
questions.stem: A 50-year-old man is diagnosed with biliary infection by Clonorchis sinensis after presenting with cholangitis and eosinophilia. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line pharmacotherapy?

explanation.summary: Praziquantel is first-line for Clonorchis and most liver flukes (Fasciola being the exception).
explanation.whyCorrect: Praziquantel is the treatment of choice for Clonorchis sinensis and most trematode infections.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Metronidazole treats amebic abscess, not fluke infection.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Fluconazole treats Candida, not trematodes.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Triclabendazole is reserved for Fasciola hepatica, which resists praziquantel; it is not first-line for Clonorchis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Ivermectin treats certain nematodes, not liver flukes.

questions.topicName: Infectious Hepatic Abscesses and Flukes
questions.stem: A 45-year-old traveler is found to have a solitary right-lobe hepatic lesion with positive amebic serology. If the lesion were aspirated, which of the following findings would best distinguish it from a pyogenic abscess?

explanation.summary: Amebic aspirate is sterile, odorless 'anchovy-paste' material, unlike the culturable pus of a pyogenic abscess.
explanation.whyCorrect: Amebic liver abscess classically yields sterile, odorless reddish-brown 'anchovy-paste' fluid (necrotic hepatocytes), distinguishing it from the foul, culturable pus of a pyogenic abscess.

whyWrongByChoice.B: Foul culturable pus describes the pyogenic abscess being distinguished from.
whyWrongByChoice.C: Clear fluid with malignant cells suggests a cystic neoplasm, not an amebic abscess.
whyWrongByChoice.D: Bile-stained fluid with ova points to biliary fluke disease, not amebiasis.
whyWrongByChoice.E: Caseous acid-fast material indicates tuberculosis, not amebiasis.
